question: In the context of the Revolt of 1857, Mangal Pandey belonged to which Bengal native Infantry?
solution:
The correct answer is __**34th Bengal Native Infantry**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mangal Pandey** was a soldier in the 34th Bengal Native Infantry.
 
• He played a significant role in the early stages of the **Revolt of 1857**, which is also known as the First War of Indian Independence.
 
• His actions on March 29, 1857, against the British officers marked a pivotal moment in the uprising.
 
• Mangal Pandey's defiance is often considered a spark that ignited the broader rebellion against British rule in India.
 
• He was subsequently arrested and executed, becoming a symbol of resistance and martyrdom in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Revolt of 1857** was a major, but ultimately unsuccessful, uprising in India against the rule of the British East India Company.
 
• The revolt began on May 10, 1857, in the town of Meerut and soon spread to other regions.
 
• It was characterized by widespread mutinies, civil rebellion, and other forms of resistance.
 
• While the revolt did not achieve its goal of ending British rule, it marked a significant turning point in Indian history and led to major changes in how India was governed.
 
• Following the revolt, the British Crown took direct control of India from the East India Company, leading to the establishment of the British Raj.
